newsitem.title: FRANCE: French centre-right would win majority - poll.
newsitem.headline: French centre-right would win majority - poll.

text.p: Following are the results of an opinion poll of voters' intentions ahead of the May 25/June 1 French parliamentary election.
The telephone poll of 1,620 adults aged 18 and over was conducted by IPSOS on April 29 and 30 for the weekly Le Point and made public on May 1:
In the previous parliament, the Communists held 24 seats, the Socialists and their left-wing allies 76, while the UDF and RPR had 477 seats.

IPSOS said 22 percent of those surveyed did not say how they would vote. In the survey, 60 percent said their party choice was definite, while 40 percent said they could still change their voting plans.

In the last poll IPSOS conducted on April 22 and 23, it found that 1.5 percent supported the extreme left, 10 percent favoured the Communists, 29 percent backed the Socialists and other leftist groups, five percent would vote for ecologist candidates, 39.5 percent were supporters of the RPR/UDF and other right-wing parties while the Front National had the backing of 15 percent.
The poll showed that slightly more voters approved of the way Prime Minister Alain Juppe had run his campaign compared with Socialist Party leader Lioinel Jospin.

Some 25 percent of those surveyed believed Juppe had run a better campaign against 22 percent for Jospin. Some 15 percent, however, believed neither had run a good campaign, while 38 percent gave no opinion. In the previous April 22-23 survey, 27 percent thought Jospin had run a better campaign against 21 percent for Juppe. In that survey, eight percent believed neither had run a good campaign and 44 percent had no opinion.
Nineteen percent of the respondents believed that if the centre-right won re-election, Juppe should remain prime minister, while 65 percent wanted him replaced. Sixteen percent had no opinion.
For 67 percent of those surveyed, the government's economic record was either decisive or important to them in determining the way they would vote.
